title: ASSD: Attentive Single Shot Multibox Detector

problem.summary: One-stage detectors are fast but less accurate than two-stage detectors, largely because of foreground/background imbalance among dense anchors, while existing fixes such as RetinaNet's focal loss are parameter sensitive and heavier SSD refinements (DSSD/FSSD) cost computation.
statements: One-stage detectors are generally less accurate than two-stage detectors, mainly due to extreme foreground-background class imbalance of dense anchor boxes.
RetinaNet's focal loss is parameter sensitive and needs exhaustive experiments to tune.
SSD's shallow feature layers lack semantic information and are insufficient for detecting small objects.

evidence.quote: However, the one-stage detectors are generally less accurate than the two-stage ones. The main reason would be the extreme foreground-background class imbalance of the dense anchor boxes [18].
However, the focal loss is parameter sensitive, and it would require exhaustive experiments to obtain the optimal parameters.
However, the shallow layer lacks semantic information and is therefore insufficient for detecting small objects.

background.summary: ASSD builds on SSD as the base one-stage detector, contrasts with DSSD's complex feature pyramid and FSSD's fusion modules, and adapts Transformer-style self-attention plus prior contextual-attention work (AC-CNN, LPA, RelationNet) to pixel-level feature relations.

relatedWork.name: SSD
relatedWork.relation: base detector chosen for its speed/accuracy/simplicity trade-off
relatedWork.quote: We choose the SSD as our base one-stage detector, which provides the optimal trade-off among simplicity, speed and accuracy.

relatedWork.name: DSSD
relatedWork.relation: prior SSD refinement using a complex feature pyramid at higher computational cost
relatedWork.quote: DSSD [5] relies on a complex feature pyramid to encourage the information flow among different layers.

relatedWork.name: FSSD
relatedWork.relation: prior fusion-module refinement with only marginal gains over SSD
relatedWork.quote: Another recent approach, FSSD [16], builds additional fusion modules for multi-scale feature aggregation, but only achieves marginal improvements upon SSD.

relatedWork.name: Transformer
relatedWork.relation: source of the self-attention mechanism adapted to feature maps
relatedWork.quote: Transformer [29] draws global dependencies between input and output based solely on attention mechanisms.

relatedWork.name: RelationNet
relatedWork.relation: proposal-level attention prior work limited to two-stage detectors
relatedWork.quote: RelationNet correlates the geometry features and appearance information between proposals to generate and forward the attentive features, and it is designed specifically for the two-stage object detectors.

evidence.quote: Two-stage object detectors are quite effective at object feature learning. However, they are generally inefficient in computation.
Compared to methods that only build relations among proposals [11, 31], our method considers the global feature correlations at pixel level and conforms to the visual mechanism of humans.

solution.summary: ASSD embeds a small fully differentiable attention unit between SSD's feature maps and prediction heads: it projects features to queries/keys/values, builds an NxN softmax attention map of pixel-level relations, and adds the reweighted features back residually, optionally after fusing semantics from deeper layers into conv3.
solution.approach: Use a Transformer-style self-attention unit on each SSD feature map to highlight useful regions and suppress irrelevant ones before box regression and classification, keeping SSD's overall structure.
components: attention unit with query/key/value projections (C' = C/8) and softmax attention map
residual feature update x_s = x_s + (a_s v(x_s)^T)^T
semantic fusion of conv4 and conv5 into conv3 with bilinear upsampling and 1x1 conv
ResNet101 backbone with SSD-style extra blocks conv6-9
hard negative mining and SSD anchor/loss settings unchanged

evidence.quote: The proposed network, termed ASSD, builds feature relations in the spatial space of the feature map.
This design generates the attention maps which highlight the useful regions and suppress the irrelevant information.
we construct a small network, namely attention unit, and embed it into SSD to improve the detection accuracy.
It highlights the relevant parts of the feature map and guides the detection with refined information.

experiments.summary: ASSD is evaluated on PASCAL VOC 2007/2012 test and COCO 2017 test-dev against SSD, DSSD, FSSD, RetinaNet, RefineDet and two-stage detectors, with an ablation separating the attention unit from semantic fusion and a visualization of the learned attention maps.

evidence.quote: Experimental results show that ASSD competes favorably with the state-of-the-arts, including SSD, DSSD, FSSD and RetinaNet.
As shown in Table 2, with a comparable fast speed, ASSD achieves a large improvement in accuracy compared to SSD, DSSD, and FSSD.
when the intersection over union (IoU) is higher than 0.5, ASSD513 has a 2.4% improvement compared to RetinaNet500.

limitations.summary: The gains come with extra compute, the fusion component alone does not help, and ASSD keeps SSD's dense anchors and hard negative mining rather than redesigning label assignment.
items: Semantic fusion alone does not notably improve accuracy and adds computational overhead.
The full attention+fusion model runs slower than plain SSD513 (0.1648s vs 0.1417s per image on a K40).
ASSD retains SSD's anchor boxes and hard negative mining, so the dense-anchor design and its imbalance issue are mitigated rather than removed.

evidence.quote: we find the fusion operation alone does not notably improve the detection accuracy (see Table 3).
Instead, it even decreases the accuracy a bit with more computational cost.
We use hard negative mining to solve the positive-negative box class imbalance problem as in the original SSD [21].

applications.detail: the one-stage design is motivated by the need for detectors usable in real-time settings where two-stage pipelines are too slow
applications.quote: However, these two-stage object detectors are inefficient for real-time applications due to the decoupled multi-stage processing.
